issue.close_reason: Verified: cargo build --lib succeeded. cargo test --lib source:: -> 31 passed, 0 failed (1 new: collect_normalized_http_refuses_a_redirect_instead_of_following_it -- runs a real loopback server that responds 302 to a second 'redirect target' server, asserts collect() returns Err, and asserts the target server never receives a connection, proving the redirect is refused rather than followed). Outcome: all HTTP requests this program makes (Anthropic OAuth usage/refresh and normalized_http) now have redirects disabled via a single shared http_agent()/reject_redirect() chokepoint, closing plan.md §7.4's redirect-policy requirement for both the credential-bearing native path and generic normalized_http.
issue.description: Disable redirects entirely for credential-bearing native requests (Anthropic OAuth); disable or restrict to same-origin for normalized_http generic sources. §7.4.
issue.notes: http_agent() (the single shared HTTP builder for both the credential-bearing Anthropic path and normalized_http) now sets .redirects(0) unconditionally -- picking the stricter of the plan's two permitted options ('disabled' or 'same-origin-only') uniformly rather than hand-rolling same-origin redirect comparison logic. Verified against ureq 2.12.1 source (unit.rs line 165) that redirects==0 unconditionally returns the 3xx response as Ok before any of the 307/308 method-preservation logic runs, so a legitimate credential-bearing POST (refresh_anthropic) is also covered, not just GETs. Because ureq returns Ok(response) with a 3xx status rather than Err when redirects are disabled, added a shared reject_redirect() helper applied at all three HTTP call sites (collect_normalized_http, the Anthropic usage GET, refresh_anthropic's POST) that turns a 3xx into an explicit, clear Err instead of an opaque JSON-parse failure.
issue.title: Enforce redirect policy for credential-bearing vs normalized HTTP requests

issue.close_reason: Added a command timeout and process-group termination for both CommandObserver and CommandActuator per plan.md §11.1/§11.2: children now spawn as the leader of their own process group (std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::process_group(0)); a 15s CHILD_TIMEOUT ceiling is enforced via poll-based wait_with_timeout for the actuator (no output capture) and a background reader thread + recv_timeout for the observer (needed since the size-bounded stdout read must keep consuming bytes concurrently with the deadline); on timeout or size-overflow, kill_child_tree uses nix::sys::signal::killpg to kill the whole group, not just the direct child, replacing the single-PID child.kill() from the prior hardening pass. Added nix as a new unix-only dependency (target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies; already a transitive dep of ctrlc). Non-unix builds fall back to plain child.kill(), matching state.rs's existing #[cfg(unix)]/#[cfg(not(unix))] pattern. Timeout is a parameter on the private command_observer_current_workers/command_actuator_actuate functions so tests use short timeouts (100-500ms) instead of the real 15s. Added tests proving both the timing (hanging sleep 5 returns Err around 100ms) and, critically, process-group semantics: a backgrounded grandchild that would write a marker file after 300ms never does, because group-kill takes it down with the direct child -- this is the test that would have failed under the old single-PID kill. issue.close_reason: main() now returns std::process::ExitCode instead of relying on anyhow's default (uniform exit-1) main-return handling. Introduced GovernorError{CliOrConfig,State,Source,Actuation} wrapping the underlying anyhow::Error, mapping 1:1 to the §12 table (2/3/4/5); the top-level handler prints one structured fatal_error JSONL event (event/time/exit_code/error) and returns the matching ExitCode. Config::load and CLI dispatch live in a new run_cli(): config-load and unknown-account errors map to CliOrConfig(2); snapshot's source::collect/serialization failures map to Source(4); run()'s StateLock::acquire/State::load/State::save/signal-handler-install failures map to State(3). Per-account failures inside run_cycle are now categorized via a new AccountFailure enum (Observation vs Actuation) instead of one undifferentiated Result, so run --once picks Actuation(5) over Source(4) when both occur in a cycle, matching the table's exit-5-for-actuation intent; each account_error JSONL event now also carries category and a UTC time field per §13's 'every event must contain event, account when applicable, and a UTC timestamp' (the pre-existing decision event's schema is unchanged -- that stabilization is separately tracked by open bead subgov-e3118a52). CodexSession gained last_result/last_reconciled_at/last_observed_at fields. New codex_cache_is_usable(last_result, last_reconciled_at, now) decides whether a poll can be answered from cache (true only when a cached result exists AND CODEX_RECONCILE_INTERVAL=900s has not elapsed since the last *full read* -- notifications update the cached value but never reset this clock, so a notification stream alone can never indefinitely postpone reconciliation). capture_codex_notification() recognizes id-less account/rateLimits/updated messages and caches their params; drain_pending_codex_notifications() non-blockingly applies any pending ones before each poll; receive_codex_response() (renamed from receive_response) also captures notifications interleaved while awaiting a specific response id. Critically, observed_at is now threaded through (with_codex_session/codex_session_read_rate_limits return (Value, DateTime<Utc>) instead of just Value) so a cache-served poll reports the TRUE time its data was obtained, not Utc::now() -- otherwise the plan.md §9.1 freshness gate (now - observed_at > stale_after_seconds) would be fooled into treating stale cached data as fresh. Verified: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib passes 226/226 including 3 new codex_cache_is_usable unit tests (requires-cache, accepts-recent-full-read, expires-after-interval, using synthetic Instant arithmetic -- no real sleep needed); cargo test --test codex_app_server_contract passes 11/11. EVIDENCE (codinghome, 2026-10-07). Banked Codex reset credit 8a8b expired UNREDEEMED at 2026-10-05T04:19Z. No governor was deployed or watching, so nothing flagged it. Three facts made it unavoidable and none was visible to any tool: (1) the provider zeroed the weekly window out of cycle on 09-26 16:58, 10-02 12:42, 10-02 21:13 and 10-07 03:28Z (resets_at moved with credits unchanged; 10-07: 92% -> 1%), re-basing every deadline each time -- at the 10-02 21:13 reset the credit had 55h left and needed ~2.0%/h while the fleet burned ~0.5%/h, i.e. it was already infeasible 55h before expiry; (2) the Codex roster shrank 15 -> 6 workers with no alarm; (3) the aggregate account is also consumed by operator/interactive Codex sessions (a +20-point jump in 3h on 10-06 with 6 workers), so per-worker burn is not stable.
Simulation (pace_sim, 1h steps, real deadlines 10-22 20:35Z and 10-29 18:53Z, window 4% used, resets 10-14 03:28Z, human redeems at 100%): constant pace 0.4%/h loses BOTH credits (214 pts consumed); 0.6%/h loses none if redemption is prompt, both if redemption lags 12h; 0.8-1.0%/h loses none either way; >=1.5%/h saturates at ~496 pts by 10-29 and extra workers only add blocked hours. After credits are spent, steady pace = 100/168 = 0.6%/h plus the share needed for newly granted credits (grants so far: 09-04, 09-05, 09-22, 09-29 -> ~0.85/week => ~1.1%/h long run).
SPEC: (1) Per-credit deadline slack: slack_i = hours_to_expiry_i - safety - need_i/burn, need_i = (target-used) + i*target for credits sorted by expiry (existing subgov formula), burn = measured AGGREGATE %/h over a >=24h baseline (quantized percent; never a 2-sample delta). Recompute on every resets_at/generation change. Emit advisory events at slack<48h (warn), <12h (page), <0 (infeasible: state the pace that WOULD work and the max feasible pace) and notify the operator. (2) Pace target = max(natural-window pace x multiplier floor, max_i need_i/(hours_to_expiry_i - safety)); publish required_burn_per_hour and a feasible flag. (3) Never redeem, never expose a redeem path (unchanged); the advisory fires manual_redemption_recommended at >=redeem_at_utilization. (4) Cap desired workers at eligible-backlog capacity: quota headroom alone is not a reason to run workers (org Productive Work rule). (5) Separate exogenous (operator/interactive) burn from governed-worker burn before computing per-worker rate. (6) Acceptance: a fixture replaying the 10-02 21:13 reset with credit 8a8b (exp 10-05 04:19) must raise an infeasible/warn advisory >=48h before expiry, and the 10-07 03:28 out-of-cycle reset must re-base slack within one poll.

issue.close_reason: Found and fixed a real correctness bug affecting all 5 places in the codebase that compare a resets_at timestamp from one poll against a stored sample from another poll for same-generation detection (controller.rs lines ~175, ~348, ~556/565; state.rs line ~293). Root cause: the real Anthropic usage API computes resets_at dynamically per request rather than returning a fixed stored timestamp, so two live polls of the same reset generation return sub-second-jittered values (confirmed live 2026-10-08 across 10 consecutive real polls of the same five_hour window: .051247Z, .130047Z, .995687Z, .771238Z, .326798Z, .209942Z, .803958Z, .522762Z, .590247Z, .123608Z -- never identical). Exact DateTime equality therefore never matched two real samples of the same generation, silently defeating: LinearToReset burn-rate learning (stuck on learning_burn_rate forever against the live account -- this is what the user asked me to investigate), banked-reset credit alert de-duplication (every poll looked like a fresh generation), the long-baseline aggregate burn estimator (every interval misclassified as spanning a reset), and bounded per-generation sample history (discarded and restarted every single cycle, never accumulating past 1 sample). Went undetected because every existing unit test and trace simulation constructs resets_at as a fixed DateTime literal reused byte-for-byte across synthetic samples, which matches trivially -- this is the first time this logic ran against the real live API. Fix: added same_reset_generation() to model.rs (60-second tolerance, documented with the real observed jitter data and why 60s is safe -- 300x margin below the shortest real reset interval, five_hour's 18000s), replaced all 5 exact-equality call sites. Added 3 new regression tests (controller::tests::learns_per_worker_burn_and_paces_despite_resets_at_jitter, controller::tests::a_genuinely_different_generation_is_not_treated_as_jitter, state::tests::record_accumulates_history_despite_resets_at_jitter) using deliberately jittered resets_at literals, unlike every pre-existing test. Verified by mutation: reverted same_reset_generation to exact equality, confirmed both new controller/state tests fail as expected, restored the fix. Verified: cargo build clean, cargo test 287 lib tests + all contract suites passing (0 failures; one fleet::needle test flaked once under parallel execution, confirmed passing in isolation and on a clean re-run of the full suite), cargo fmt and cargo clippy clean for all 3 changed files. Deployed the fix to the live subgov.service (rebuilt release binary, reinstalled, restarted -- KillMode=process correctly kept the live worker's PID unchanged through the restart) and verified directly against the real account: the very next real cycle changed from reason=learning_burn_rate (stuck forever under the old code) to reason=no_observed_burn (correctly finding and comparing against the prior sample now; no_observed_burn rather than paced_to_reset only because real usage happens to be flat between these two particular polls, which is the designed-correct classification for quantized/censored data, not a remaining bug).
issue.title: Fix exact resets_at equality breaking same-generation detection against live jittery API timestamps

issue.description: Lock refresh writes to ~/.claude/.credentials.json, or otherwise prove safe coexistence with a concurrently-running Claude Code process writing the same file. §7.1.
issue.notes: Implemented: obtain_access_token() now takes an exclusive OS advisory lock (fs2 flock, bounded retry up to timeout_seconds) on the actual ~/.claude/.credentials.json for the whole read-decide-refresh critical section, serializing against a cooperating concurrent writer (another subgov instance, or Claude Code if it also locks). Because a non-cooperating writer cannot be bound by our lock alone, the refresh result is never written blindly: apply_refreshed_credentials() re-reads the file immediately before the write and compares the refresh token the network call consumed against what is currently on disk. A mismatch means Claude Code (or another process) already rotated it while our HTTP round-trip was in flight; in that case we discard our own refresh and either return the now-current still-fresh access token or fail this poll cycle only -- we never clobber a concurrent legitimate rotation, which would otherwise strand Claude Code on an already-consumed refresh token. Unknown JSON fields in the credentials document are preserved through the CAS write.
issue.title: Lock Anthropic credential refresh writes against Claude Code

issue.close_reason: Migration from claude-governor to subgov is complete, stable, and now re-hardened. claude-governor.service stopped and disabled; subgov.service is the sole live actuating governor for anthropic:local-subscription, running a real worker (verified: same PID surviving 15+ minutes of real EXECUTING/HANDLING states across a restart). Re-added security hardening incrementally and tested each batch against a disposable probe-only unit plus the real live worker (never trusting a probe-only pass alone, per the PrivateTmp false-positive found along the way). Found and fixed a genuinely serious, independent bug in the process: KillMode=control-group (systemd's default) was killing the whole unit's cgroup -- including the dispatched worker's tmux session, which lives inside subgov.service's own cgroup, not a separate needle-worker@ unit -- on every restart. This silently destroyed a real 20-minute productive worker once during this session before being caught. Fixed with KillMode=process; verified the worker's PID is now identical before and after a real systemctl restart. Final hardening set: KillMode=process, the full kernel/namespace Protect*/Restrict* set, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, RestrictAddressFamilies, RestrictSUIDSGID, RemoveIPC, UMask, NoNewPrivileges. Permanently excluded with documented reasons: CapabilityBoundingSet=/AmbientCapabilities= (this host's container context lacks CAP_SETPCAP for unprivileged user units -- fails the unit to start outright), MemoryDenyWriteExecute (breaks the Node.js/V8-based claude CLI's JIT), ProtectSystem/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp (the spawned worker is a roaming autonomous coding agent that writes across arbitrary repos under $HOME and needs the real shared /tmp/needle -- structural exceptions, not gaps). Disposable test unit removed. Full history in docs/notes/runbooks/controller-ownership.md.

issue.description:
docs/notes/compatibility.md promises that a field slated for removal 'stays functional, with a deprecation warning, for at least one minor release before it is deleted,' but no open bead implements or tests a deprecation path, and strict deny_unknown_fields parsing leaves no place for one to live implicitly. Add a deliberate mechanism: a deprecated-field registry keyed by config schema version inside config parsing that emits a warning when a deprecated field is present (on config load and via `subgov check`) while the field continues to function until its documented removal. Add tests proving (a) a field marked deprecated still parses and keeps its effect, (b) `subgov check` reports the deprecation warning, and (c) unknown-field rejection behavior is unchanged for fields that were never introduced. This can be landed before the first field is actually deprecated so the compatibility promise is enforceable rather than aspirational.

issue.description:
The runbooks document exit codes as an operator-facing contract that monitoring and rollback automation key off: `run --once` exits 4 on a failed quota observation (cited in authentication-expiry.md and the stale-sources runbook), exit 3 on state ownership loss, and `subgov preflight` exits 2 on a malformed/conflicting inventory. Existing open beads cover only slices: subgov-1c2b1bf9 implements the exit-code table, subgov-e76aac77 tests the state-lock exit code (exit 3 only), and subgov-e954e7e7/subgov-cdce698a cover preflight's exit 2. No bead tests that a failing source produces exit 4 from `run --once` with the documented `account_error` event (category: observation) and no actuation, nor that the codes remain stable in multi-account runs where only one account fails. Add those tests, and consolidate the exit codes currently scattered across runbooks into a single documented table in the operator docs so the contract operators rely on is stated once, normatively.

issue.notes: http_agent() (src/source.rs, the single chokepoint all HTTP calls go through: collect_normalized_http, the Anthropic usage request, and refresh_anthropic) is now fallible: it bails if timeout_seconds == 0 instead of silently building an agent with a degenerate/meaningless timeout, and all three call sites propagate via '?'. Config's serde default for NormalizedHttp.timeout_seconds is already 15 (non-zero), so this only fires on an explicit operator misconfiguration. Confirmed via ureq 2.12.1 source (agent.rs) that .timeout() covers the whole request (connect through body read) and ureq has no special-casing of a zero Duration as 'unbounded' -- so this wasn't a silent-hang risk, but a zero timeout_seconds is still a nonsensical config that should fail loudly rather than produce a source that always errors instantly for the wrong reason. Also verified and regression-tested that collect_normalized_http never attaches an Authorization/Cookie header (it has no credential material in scope at all) by capturing the raw request bytes off a real loopback socket.

issue.close_reason: Implemented src/placement.rs: place() per plan.md §22.7, a pure function (no I/O) distributing an account_target across config.fleet.hosts by headroom = min(cpu_available_fraction, (mem_available_mb-mem_reserve_mb)/mem_total_mb) clamped [0,1] (host with no resource_source always headroom=1, §22.2). Eligible hosts get a floor-based proportional share (deliberately floor, not round-half-up, so sum(shares) never exceeds account_target -- round-half-up can overshoot, e.g. two 0.5-weight hosts with target=3 round to 2+2=4) with largest-remainder redistribution to hosts with ceiling headroom, ties broken by ascending host key. Ineligible (stale/unobserved) hosts get raw target 0 but are stepped down via existing max_scale_up/down_per_cycle rather than force-killed (§22.8 'frozen not drained'). When zero hosts are eligible, every host holds exactly at current (never scales up blind). A host with a configured resource_source but no entry in the caller-supplied resources map is treated as unobserved/never-eligible, same as stale. Registered as pub mod placement in src/lib.rs. Verified: cargo build (clean), cargo test placement:: -- 14/14 passing including 2 proptest properties (distributed total never exceeds account_target; ineligible hosts never receive a positive share) and unit tests for every §22.7/§22.8 boundary case named in WP10 (no eligible host, single host, ceiling-clamped host, remainder redistribution + tie-break, stale host frozen-not-drained, step-limited scale-up, determinism, zero-mem-total edge case). cargo fmt and cargo clippy clean for src/placement.rs specifically. Classification: run_cycle's existing Decision/AccountFailure values are mapped by readiness_for_decision/readiness_for_failure -- stale=true -> stale_drain; a window reason of target_reached or banked_resets.manual_redemption_recommended -> intentional_hold (reason 'target_reached'); AccountFailure::Observation -> provider_failure; AccountFailure::Actuation -> actuation_failure; otherwise healthy_learning, with the reason taken from decision.binding_window (added by subgov-ac345750, landed concurrently) resolved back to its WindowDecision.reason.

status itself only reads the locally-written status.json -- it never touches a source, observer, actuator, or credential, satisfying the DoD's "without inspecting credentials"; an account never yet cycled reports state:unknown. merge_status_report reads-modify-writes so accounts not touched by the current cycle (e.g. abandoned mid-cycle by a shutdown signal, subgov-c92d2d8b) keep their last known status instead of reverting to unknown; a corrupt/missing prior file is tolerated by starting empty, since this is a derived, best-effort surface, not durable state -- a write failure is logged (status_write_error) but never fails the run loop or changes its exit code.

Added a command timeout and process-group termination for both CommandObserver and CommandActuator per plan.md §11.1/§11.2: children now spawn as the leader of their own process group (std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::process_group(0)); a 15s CHILD_TIMEOUT ceiling is enforced via poll-based wait_with_timeout for the actuator (no output capture) and a background reader thread + recv_timeout for the observer (needed since the size-bounded stdout read must keep consuming bytes concurrently with the deadline); on timeout or size-overflow, kill_child_tree uses nix::sys::signal::killpg to kill the whole group, not just the direct child, replacing the single-PID child.kill() from the prior hardening pass. Timeout is a parameter on the private command_observer_current_workers/command_actuator_actuate functions so tests use short timeouts (100-500ms) instead of the real 15s. Added tests proving both the timing (hanging sleep 5 returns Err around 100ms) and, critically, process-group semantics: a backgrounded grandchild that would write a marker file after 300ms never does, because group-kill takes it down with the direct child -- this is the test that would have failed under the old single-PID kill. detail.title: Fix stale quarantine claim in state-backup-and-removal.md

detail.reason: Corrected docs/notes/state-backup-and-removal.md: the doc previously said the plan's quarantine-malformed-state item was still open, but a concurrent tab (subgov-d5236b6d) landed it in src/state.rs while this repo's own bead work was in flight. Replaced the stale claim with an accurate description: State::load renames an unparseable state.json aside to <name>.corrupt-<timestamp>-<pid>, preserves its bytes, proceeds with fresh default state, and run/run --once logs a state_quarantined JSONL event to stderr (verified against current src/state.rs and src/main.rs). Added a quarantine table row and a dedicated recovery subsection. Verification: cargo build succeeded; cargo test --lib state:: passed 26/26 including the new quarantine tests.

Added 5 crash-consistency/corruption tests to src/state.rs exercising each write boundary from §10: (1) crash_before_any_write_leaves_original_state_untouched_and_no_temp_file -- parent dir made read-only so temp-file create_new fails before any byte is written, proving no partial artifact and original state untouched; (2) crash_after_write_before_rename_leaves_original_state_loadable -- covers both after-write-before-fsync and after-fsync-before-rename (indistinguishable to a reader since path hasn't moved), a complete payload is written+fsynced to the temp path without renaming, proving load() ignores the orphaned temp file and returns the last-renamed state; (3) crash_mid_write_leaves_a_truncated_temp_file_but_original_state_is_still_loadable -- a half-written temp file with no fsync/rename, proving a mid-write crash never corrupts what load() returns; (4) crash_after_rename_before_directory_fsync_new_state_is_already_loadable -- reproduces save()'s write+fsync+rename sequence directly (via the same private temporary_path/OpenOptions helpers), deliberately skipping sync_directory, proving the new state is already loadable once rename lands regardless of directory-fsync timing; (5) corrupt_file_recovery_quarantines_a_truncated_mid_write_artifact_found_at_the_live_path -- half a valid JSON payload written directly to the live path (not a temp file), proving State::load quarantines it via the Quarantined machinery from subgov-d5236b6d rather than erroring raw or accepting a partial value. Verified: cargo build clean; cargo test --lib state:: -> 26 passed (one earlier run hit a transient ENOSPC/StorageFull under concurrent box load on an unrelated pre-existing test, reproduced as non-reproducible in isolation and on immediate re-run -- confirmed environmental flake, not a defect); full cargo test unaffected outside state module; rustfmt --check on state.rs shows only pre-existing unrelated drift (lines 163/209/226/264/310/330, none touched by this change); cargo clippy --lib clean except the pre-existing unrelated source.rs large_enum_variant warning.

Added FakeObserver in src/testsupport/fake_fleet.rs: an in-memory, scripted Observer implementation (push_workers/push_error over a VecDeque, panics when the script is exhausted), mirroring FakeSource's convention. Verified with cargo build (clean) and cargo test testsupport::fake_fleet (4/4 passing: returns_scripted_worker_counts_in_order, returns_scripted_errors, interleaves_successes_and_failures_in_push_order, panics_when_the_script_runs_out). Committed as b1a6078 and pushed to origin/main.

Added 3 state-migration tests to src/state.rs proving a governor started against every schema-version shape this binary actually supports reading migrates cleanly (WP3): (1) migrates_a_legacy_pre_versioning_file_and_preserves_its_data -- writes a real v0.1-baseline-shaped JSON file (no schema_version key, no history key on the account, matching what existed before subgov-d5236b6d/ec6c06db's wave), loads it via State::load, and asserts it is NOT quarantined, schema_version migrates to STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION in memory, and the account's windows/last_target data survives intact with history defaulting empty; (2) migrated_legacy_state_persists_the_current_schema_version_once_saved -- loads the same legacy shape, calls save(), then re-parses the raw bytes on disk (bypassing State::load's own defaulting) to prove the migration is sticky, i.e. the file now explicitly carries schema_version rather than relying on the reader to re-infer it every time; (3) explicit_current_schema_version_loads_without_migration_or_quarantine -- an explicit schema_version:1 file with full account data round-trips as a no-op migration. Confirmed a version newer than STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION remains out of scope for migration and stays covered by the existing load_refuses_a_newer_schema_version hard-failure test. Verified: cargo build clean; cargo test --lib state:: -> 29 passed; rustfmt --check on state.rs shows only pre-existing unrelated drift (lines 163/209/226/264/310/330); cargo clippy --lib clean except the pre-existing unrelated source.rs large_enum_variant warning.

Added 3 trace-simulation tests in src/controller.rs::tests::trace_simulations (idle, bursty, reset-heavy) per plan.md section 17.5/9.8, using the wave-1 FakeClock test double to replay week-long synthetic traces through evaluate(), closing the feedback loop like main::run_cycle (desired_workers feeds back as current_workers; non-stale snapshots fold into AccountState via record). idle_trace_holds_at_bootstrap_workers_without_runaway_scale_up: exact-zero consumption for 40 cycles/7 days must settle at bootstrap_workers and hold (censored-zero-delta guarantee extended to a long trace). bursty_trace_settles_at_target_reached_and_never_scales_up_through_a_stale_gap: irregular spikes (burst every 5th cycle) plus one injected stale gap; once a burst crosses target, target_reached is structurally permanent (used_fraction monotonic non-decreasing within one generation), and the stale gap never scales up. reset_heavy_trace_restarts_learning_each_generation_and_holds_at_the_boundary: a 5h window resetting 33 times across the week with max_workers deliberately capped so a full generation at the ceiling still can't reach target (4*0.03*5=0.6<0.8), making non-exceedance a safety-scenario property rather than tuning luck; verifies section 9.3 (no generation extrapolates a prior generation's rate; a reset the clock has passed but the provider hasn't published yet holds rather than guesses). Verification: cargo build --tests clean; cargo test --lib controller::tests::trace_simulations (3/3 pass); full suite (163 lib + 34 integration tests) passes; cargo clippy --all-targets clean (one pre-existing unrelated warning in src/source.rs, not touched by this change). Added FleetConfig.hosts: Option<BTreeMap<String, HostConfig>> plus HostConfig/ResourceReserveConfig/ResourceSourceConfig per plan.md §22.3. fleet.observer is now Option<WorkerObserverConfig>: validate_fleet() requires it when hosts is absent, rejects it (and a non-none top-level actuator) alongside hosts, requires >=1 host when hosts is present, requires resource_reserve whenever a host sets resource_source, and caps host max_workers at the account's max_workers. Verified: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib config:: (11/11 new+existing config tests pass, covering the plan's two-host example, backward-compat single-host case, and every validation error path), full cargo test suite green (151 lib + 20 main + 8 contract tests, no regressions). NOTE: heavily concurrent shared checkout (multiple Herdr tabs committing to local main every few seconds); a concurrent 'git commit --amend' collision briefly merged this bead's controller.rs fix into another tab's subgov-7d032768 commit (484085d) instead of its own clean commit. Verified no data/attribution was lost: diffed 484085d against the pre-amend baseline and against b8dc5a2, confirming it contains exactly subgov-7d032768's fixture work plus this bead's intended controller.rs diff and nothing else; a third tab's in-progress trace_simulations work that transiently leaked into my working tree was restored and later committed correctly by its owner as 6da7d0b under subgov-df87a3a8. origin/main (fa53b64 at close time) reflects all of this correctly.

Implemented the idempotency-token contract in src/fleet.rs's command_actuator_actuate(): sets SUBGOV_IDEMPOTENCY_TOKEN on the child's environment to a hex-encoded, deterministic hash (std::hash::DefaultHasher, fixed keys, stable across process restarts) of the rendered argv + desired count, documented in a doc comment specifying the full contract (optional for the script, stable across a same-desired-count retry, changes when command or desired changes, carries no quota/credential/account data). Verified with cargo build (clean) and cargo test fleet:: (36/36 passing, including 3 new pure-function tests on idempotency_token and one new integration test command_actuator_passes_the_idempotency_token_as_a_non_secret_env_var that spawns a real /bin/sh child reading $SUBGOV_IDEMPOTENCY_TOKEN). Added docs/notes/runbooks/reset-rollover.md covering §9.3 generation matching (exact resets_at equality), the reason-string sequence across a rollover (paced_to_reset -> reset_due -> bootstrap_burn_rate/learning_burn_rate -> paced_to_reset), diagnosing a stuck reset_due vs a healthy one, no_observed_burn's quantization semantics per estimate_burn_per_worker, and a pointer to ADR-0001/banked-reset manual redemption as a distinct condition. Added 3 tests to src/fleet.rs's test module proving the WP4 definition of done ('a hung or failed external helper is bounded, isolated to its account, and cannot be reported as successful actuation'): (1) a_hung_actuation_is_bounded_and_never_reported_as_successful -- a hanging command actuator times out via CHILD_TIMEOUT/wait_with_timeout well before the underlying sleep would return, and always returns Err; (2) retrying_an_unchanged_desired_count_after_a_hung_actuation_reuses_the_same_idempotency_token -- simulates plan.md sec 11.2's retained-state retry end-to-end: a hung first attempt is killed, and the identical retry (same rendered command/desired count, as happens when prior state is retained on failure) sees the same SUBGOV_IDEMPOTENCY_TOKEN (built in subgov-8aaa4207), proving the token wiring survives the real hang-and-kill path, not just the pure function; (3) a_hung_actuation_does_not_affect_an_independent_actuation -- the actuator primitives carry no shared state, so a hung actuation for one config cannot bleed into another's (per-account isolation within a single run_cycle is main.rs's own property, already covered there; this is the fleet-level guarantee enabling it). Verified with cargo build (clean for fleet.rs; pre-existing warnings in src/source.rs are from another concurrent tab's unrelated uncommitted work, not touched here) and cargo test fleet:: (39/39 passing, including the 3 new tests). Committed as 3bbbc8f and confirmed pushed to origin/main (1134b70..3bbbc8f).

Added docs/notes/runbooks/conflicting-controllers.md covering §10's 'only one controller may own a fleet' invariant: StateLock only protects two processes sharing the exact same state_path (verified against StateLock::acquire's exact 'another governor owns <path>' message and exit code 3); different-state-path or non-subgov-legacy conflicts are undetectable by subgov itself and must be caught behaviorally (oscillating current_workers, strict-mode observer_reconciliation rejections whose doc comment in src/fleet.rs explicitly names this scenario, unexplained target_file changes). Cross-linked into runbooks/README.md. Verification: cargo build succeeded; cargo test --lib fleet:: passed 39/39 plus targeted current_workers_accepts/rejects/clamps tests covering the strict/clamp reconciliation behavior documented.

Published schema/decision-event.schema.json, freezing the section 13 JSONL decision-event contract (the {event:"decision", observe_only, actuated, decision:<Decision>} line main::run_cycle prints to stdout), hand-written against src/controller.rs (Decision/WindowDecision/BankedResetDecision) and src/main.rs's emission code, following the same conventions as the existing schema/quota-snapshot.schema.json and schema/governor-config.schema.json (draft 2020-12, additionalProperties:true since the Rust structs have no deny_unknown_fields, date-time pattern backstop). Includes the WP2 binding_window field, and freezes as closed enums the two fixed sets of Rust string literals the event carries: windowDecision.reason (target_reached, reset_due, below_ceiling, paced_to_reset, no_observed_burn, bootstrap_burn_rate, learning_burn_rate) and bankedResetDecision.reason (weekly_window_awaiting_manual_redemption, banked_reset_expiry_deadline_missed, minimum_banked_reset_pace, banked_reset_expiry_pace, bootstrap_banked_reset_burn_rate, learning_banked_reset_burn_rate). Verification: (1) python3 jsonschema Draft202012Validator with format_checker, 10 hand-built valid/invalid cases (missing required decision, wrong event const, bad reason enum value, valid/invalid banked_resets sub-object requiring all its fields together, out-of-range used_fraction, boundary target_utilization exactly 0, unknown-field tolerance) all matched expected verdict. (2) Built the actual subgov binary (cargo build --bin subgov) and ran run --once --observe-only three times against a scratch normalized_file config/fixture (mutating state.json/snapshot.json between runs), capturing and validating 3 REAL emitted decision events against the schema: an ordinary learning_burn_rate decision, a paced_to_reset decision with observed_burn_per_worker_hour present, and a stale decision with empty windows -- all three passed with zero schema errors. cargo build (whole workspace) stayed clean throughout. Committed as fe1f381, pushed to origin (fast-forward, confirmed via git merge-base --is-ancestor).

Added docs/notes/runbooks/rollback.md covering WP8's 'one-command rollback to observe-only or the previous controller': (1) rollback to observe-only via --observe-only flag restart (config/CLI read once at startup, no hot-reload, verified against Cli::parse()/Config::load in run_cli), whole-process scope, learning continues since AccountState::record runs regardless of observe_only; (2) rollback to the previous controller, cross-linked to the conflicting-controllers runbook for the stop-then-start handoff sequencing; (3) single-account rollback needing a config edit + restart since --observe-only isn't per-account. Cross-linked into runbooks/README.md. Verification: cargo build succeeded; cargo test --bin subgov passed 20/20 (status_tests confirm readiness classifications, exit_code_tests confirm exit-code table).

Replaced per-poll Codex app-server spawn/kill with a supervised long-lived session in src/source.rs: sessions are cached process-wide (Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, CodexSession>>, keyed by executable path), a call reuses an existing session's live handshake and sends only account/rateLimits/read on it (JSON-RPC id continues incrementing across polls), and a broken session (dead process, closed pipe, timeout) is dropped and transparently respawned within the same call rather than surfacing a permanent failure. Split former read_codex_rate_limits into spawn_and_handshake_codex (spawn+initialize+initialized once) and codex_session_read_rate_limits (repeatable per-poll request). Added pub fn shutdown_codex_sessions() for orderly cleanup/test isolation. Bounded Codex stdout frame parsing in src/source.rs: the reader thread now uses read_bounded_codex_frame (new MAX_CODEX_FRAME_BYTES=1MiB constant) instead of unbounded BufReader::lines(). Implemented push-notification consumption with periodic full-read reconciliation in src/source.rs's CodexSession (plan.md §7.2). New codex_cache_is_usable(last_result, last_reconciled_at, now) decides whether a poll can be answered from cache (true only when a cached result exists AND CODEX_RECONCILE_INTERVAL=900s has not elapsed since the last *full read* -- notifications update the cached value but never reset this clock, so a notification stream alone can never indefinitely postpone reconciliation). capture_codex_notification() recognizes id-less account/rateLimits/updated messages and caches their params; drain_pending_codex_notifications() non-blockingly applies any pending ones before each poll; receive_codex_response() (renamed from receive_response) also captures notifications interleaved while awaiting a specific response id. Implemented src/placement.rs: place() per plan.md §22.7, a pure function (no I/O) distributing an account_target across config.fleet.hosts by headroom = min(cpu_available_fraction, (mem_available_mb-mem_reserve_mb)/mem_total_mb) clamped [0,1] (host with no resource_source always headroom=1, §22.2). Eligible hosts get a floor-based proportional share (deliberately floor, not round-half-up, so sum(shares) never exceeds account_target -- round-half-up can overshoot, e.g. two 0.5-weight hosts with target=3 round to 2+2=4) with largest-remainder redistribution to hosts with ceiling headroom, ties broken by ascending host key. Ineligible (stale/unobserved) hosts get raw target 0 but are stepped down via existing max_scale_up/down_per_cycle rather than force-killed (§22.8 'frozen not drained'). When zero hosts are eligible, every host holds exactly at current (never scales up blind). A host with a configured resource_source but no entry in the caller-supplied resources map is treated as unobserved/never-eligible, same as stale. Registered as pub mod placement in src/lib.rs. Verified: cargo build (clean), cargo test placement:: -- 14/14 passing including 2 proptest properties (distributed total never exceeds account_target; ineligible hosts never receive a positive share) and unit tests for every §22.7/§22.8 boundary case named in WP10 (no eligible host, single host, ceiling-clamped host, remainder redistribution + tie-break, stale host frozen-not-drained, step-limited scale-up, determinism, zero-mem-total edge case). cargo fmt and cargo clippy clean for src/placement.rs specifically. detail.title: Fix exact resets_at equality breaking same-generation detection against live jittery API timestamps

detail.reason: Found and fixed a real correctness bug affecting all 5 places in the codebase that compare a resets_at timestamp from one poll against a stored sample from another poll for same-generation detection (controller.rs lines ~175, ~348, ~556/565; state.rs line ~293). Root cause: the real Anthropic usage API computes resets_at dynamically per request rather than returning a fixed stored timestamp, so two live polls of the same reset generation return sub-second-jittered values (confirmed live 2026-10-08 across 10 consecutive real polls of the same five_hour window: .051247Z, .130047Z, .995687Z, .771238Z, .326798Z, .209942Z, .803958Z, .522762Z, .590247Z, .123608Z -- never identical). Exact DateTime equality therefore never matched two real samples of the same generation, silently defeating: LinearToReset burn-rate learning (stuck on learning_burn_rate forever against the live account -- this is what the user asked me to investigate), banked-reset credit alert de-duplication (every poll looked like a fresh generation), the long-baseline aggregate burn estimator (every interval misclassified as spanning a reset), and bounded per-generation sample history (discarded and restarted every single cycle, never accumulating past 1 sample). Went undetected because every existing unit test and trace simulation constructs resets_at as a fixed DateTime literal reused byte-for-byte across synthetic samples, which matches trivially -- this is the first time this logic ran against the real live API. Fix: added same_reset_generation() to model.rs (60-second tolerance, documented with the real observed jitter data and why 60s is safe -- 300x margin below the shortest real reset interval, five_hour's 18000s), replaced all 5 exact-equality call sites. Added 3 new regression tests (controller::tests::learns_per_worker_burn_and_paces_despite_resets_at_jitter, controller::tests::a_genuinely_different_generation_is_not_treated_as_jitter, state::tests::record_accumulates_history_despite_resets_at_jitter) using deliberately jittered resets_at literals, unlike every pre-existing test. Verified by mutation: reverted same_reset_generation to exact equality, confirmed both new controller/state tests fail as expected, restored the fix. Verified: cargo build clean, cargo test 287 lib tests + all contract suites passing (0 failures; one fleet::needle test flaked once under parallel execution, confirmed passing in isolation and on a clean re-run of the full suite), cargo fmt and cargo clippy clean for all 3 changed files. Deployed the fix to the live subgov.service (rebuilt release binary, reinstalled, restarted -- KillMode=process correctly kept the live worker's PID unchanged through the restart) and verified directly against the real account: the very next real cycle changed from reason=learning_burn_rate (stuck forever under the old code) to reason=no_observed_burn (correctly finding and comparing against the prior sample now; no_observed_burn rather than paced_to_reset only because real usage happens to be flat between these two particular polls, which is the designed-correct classification for quantized/censored data, not a remaining bug).
